overview: Rocket Lab is a vertically integrated end-to-end space company providing launch services and space systems solutions. The company operates the Electron small-lift rocket — the Western world's second most frequently flown orbital rocket behind SpaceX's Falcon 9, with 88+ launches completed — while developing the medium-lift reusable Neutron rocket targeting first flight in Q4 2026. Its Space Systems segment designs and manufactures satellites, spacecraft, and electro-optical/infrared (EO/IR) payloads for national security and commercial customers, representing ~68% of FY2025 revenue and underpinned by a $2.2B backlog as of March 2026.

business_model.summary: Dual-segment model: Launch Services (Electron and HASTE suborbital rockets, contract-based) and Space Systems (satellite manufacturing, spacecraft components, spacecraft buses, and now EO/IR payloads via the Geost acquisition). Revenue is primarily project/contract-based, heavily weighted toward long-duration U.S. government and defense contracts that provide multi-year visibility. The company is pre-profitability and reinvesting aggressively in Neutron development and manufacturing scale.
business_model.customer_type: B2G / B2B: U.S. government and defense (dominant and growing via SDA, Space Force, HASTE program), commercial satellite operators, international government customers
business_model.geographic_mix: United States (majority, >70%), New Zealand and international commercial (remainder). Launch infrastructure at Mahia Peninsula NZ (LC-1) and Wallops Island VA (LC-2, Neutron pad under development)

main_competitors: Firefly Aerospace (Alpha, MLV medium-lift in development, publicly listed 2025)
Relativity Space (Terran R medium-lift reusable, targeting late 2026)
United Launch Alliance (Vulcan Centaur for national security launches)
Blue Origin (New Glenn for NSSL missions)
Traditional defense primes for Space Systems (Northrop Grumman, L3Harris, Lockheed Martin, Raytheon)
competitive_position.market_position: Global leader among publicly traded pure-play space companies. Dominant in dedicated small-satellite launch (Electron is #2 orbital rocket in the West). Emerging defense prime contractor validated by $816M SDA TRKT3 award and addition to U.S. Space Force NSSL Phase 3 Lane 1 pool — one of only five providers eligible for the nation's highest-priority national security launches. Neutron targets the medium-lift market currently dominated by SpaceX's Falcon 9.

moat_factors.description: 88+ Electron launches with near-perfect reliability. Record 21 successful launches in FY2025, record 6 in Q1 2026, targeting 100th Electron launch in 2026 — the fastest commercial rocket to reach that milestone. Proven cadence is a durable advantage competitors cannot replicate quickly.

moat_factors.factor: Vertical integration across the space stack
moat_factors.description: End-to-end capabilities from launch vehicle design and manufacture, to spacecraft buses (Photon, Explorer class), to satellites, to EO/IR payloads (post-Geost). Rocket Lab can build, launch, and operate customer missions entirely in-house — a unique value proposition vs. defense primes lacking launch or commercial operators lacking manufacturing.

moat_factors.factor: Defense prime status and cleared facility access
moat_factors.description: $816M SDA TRKT3 prime contract and $1.3B+ total SDA awards validate Rocket Lab as a trusted prime. NSSL Lane 1 inclusion opens the $5.6B DoD launch pool. Cleared facilities and 20+ years of flight heritage via Geost EO/IR payloads provide classified program access barriers.

$2.2B backlog as of March 2026 (up from $1.85B in December 2025), with ~36% expected to convert to revenue in the next 12 months. Provides approximately 3 years of revenue visibility at current run rates and limits near-term revenue risk.
Two operational launch complexes (NZ and Wallops) with dedicated Neutron pad under development at Wallops. Launch site access is a regulatory and capital-intensive barrier for new entrants.

weaknesses: Neutron development behind original schedule — January 2026 Stage 1 tank failure during pressure testing (at a third-party-built joint) requires redesign, with Q4 2026 maiden flight dependent on Archimedes engine qualification

SpaceX's Falcon 9 (165 launches in 2025, 17,500kg capacity) represents a structurally dominant competitor in medium lift that Neutron (13,000kg target) must differentiate against primarily on availability and Western-sourcing preference
Pre-profitability with sustained operating losses — operating loss -$228.8M in FY2025, adjusted EBITDA still negative, path to breakeven contingent on Neutron reaching commercial cadence

Meaningful share dilution: diluted share count grew from ~505M (Q1 2025) to ~573M (Q4 2025) via equity raises; Geost acquisition added additional shares; further dilution likely as capital needs continue
Customer concentration risk within defense — SDA contracts represent a large portion of Space Systems backlog, creating exposure to government budget cycles and program sequestration

growth_drivers: Neutron medium-lift rocket: First flight targeted Q4 2026, with five launch contracts already signed for 2026-2029 missions. NSSL Lane 1 eligibility opens a $5.6B DoD launch pool; Neutron addresses a market many times larger than Electron's small-sat segment. Post-first-flight cadence plan: 1 launch in year 1, 3 in year 2, 5 in year 3.

SDA and national security Space Systems ramp: $816M TRKT3 prime contract to build 18 missile-tracking satellites (total SDA awards >$1.3B combined). Contract extends well into the decade and anchors Space Systems backlog, with potential follow-on Tranches and adjacent classified programs.

Geost/EO/IR payload integration: Closed August 2025 for $275M ($125M cash + stock + $50M earnout). Adds 20+ years of EO/IR flight heritage for missile warning, ISR, and space domain awareness — completing Rocket Lab's vertical stack from sensor to satellite to rocket. Enables new-prime bids on classified payload programs.

Electron cadence expansion and HASTE: Record 21 launches in FY2025; on track to exceed that in FY2026 targeting 100th launch milestone. $190M HASTE hypersonic test vehicle contract (20 launches) adds a new revenue stream in the suborbital market. Launch manifest >70 missions.

Backlog conversion: $2.2B backlog as of March 2026, ~36% converting in next 12 months implying $790M+ near-term contracted revenue, well above current annualized pace — supports continued YoY revenue growth.

NASA and scientific missions as proof-of-concept: ESCAPADE Mars twin spacecraft (built by Rocket Lab, launched November 2025, en route to Mars orbit 2027) and Venus Life Finder mission demonstrate Photon spacecraft bus capability for interplanetary science, validating next-gen Explorer class spacecraft for future NASA opportunities.

Secular tailwinds in LEO mega-constellations: Growing demand for small and medium satellite manufacturing and launch tied to proliferated commercial and government constellations (Starlink, Kuiper, PWSA) drives sustained backlog replenishment.

business.description: A further slip past Q4 2026 or an anomaly on first flight would undercut the medium-lift revenue thesis, cede market positioning to Firefly MLV and Terran R, and likely compress the premium valuation multiple significantly. The stock's re-rating since early 2026 is substantially pricing in Neutron success.

Falcon 9 launched 165 times in 2025 — six times more than all other U.S. providers combined — with aggressive pricing and proven full reusability. SpaceX Starship could further commoditize medium and heavy lift. Neutron must win on Western-source preference, schedule reliability, and dedicated mission flexibility rather than price.

Firefly Aerospace (now publicly listed, targeting $435M revenue in 2026) and Relativity Space's Terran R are both targeting overlapping market segments. If either achieves commercial flight before Neutron or at lower price points, Neutron's launch manifest could be cannibalized before it flies.

SDA TRKT3 ($816M) and related programs represent a substantial share of Space Systems backlog. A program restructure, Congressional budget sequestration, or technical performance issue on the 18-satellite constellation could materially affect multi-year revenue projections.

financial.description: FY2025 operating loss -$228.8M; Q1 2026 net loss -$45M. Neutron development requires continued heavy R&D spend. Equity raises have grown share count >13% in FY2025 alone. At a ~$50B+ market cap (at ~$98/share), further dilutive raises are possible to fund Geost integration, Neutron pad construction, and manufacturing scale.

Stock appreciated ~3x from ~$31 (early February 2026) to ~$98 (current, 52-week high $151). Consensus price target ~$103-107, implying modest upside from current levels. The multiple embeds a successful Neutron debut and sustained 35-40%+ revenue growth — any execution miss risks sharp multiple compression.

Adjusted EBITDA remains negative ($20-26M loss guided for Q2 2026). Positive free cash flow likely requires Neutron at commercial cadence (3-5 flights per year), which is realistically a 2028+ milestone even under an optimistic scenario.

regulatory.description: Neutron's first launch from Wallops Island requires FAA environmental review and launch license. Any delays in the regulatory process could extend first-flight timelines independently of technical readiness.

Geost's EO/IR payloads and Neutron's capabilities are highly sensitive under ITAR. Strict export compliance limits international customer addressable market and adds overhead to non-U.S. commercial contracts. The company's New Zealand operations require careful licensing management.

regulatory.risk: Space debris and orbital sustainability regulations
regulatory.description: Emerging FCC and international regulations on deorbit requirements and spectrum coordination could add compliance costs to satellite manufacturing and launch programs.

macro.description: SDA and Space Force contracts are subject to Congressional appropriations. Continuing resolutions, sequestration, or shifting defense priorities (e.g., program restructuring of PWSA) could delay contract payments or reduce total contract values.

As a pre-profitability high-growth company trading at elevated multiples, RKLB is sensitive to interest rate levels affecting discount rates and growth stock valuations broadly. Rate increases compress multiples disproportionately for pre-earnings companies.

Carbon fiber composites, specialized rocket propulsion components, advanced sensors, and semiconductor content are subject to supply chain disruptions. Customer spacecraft delays (as seen in Q3 2025) can cascade into Electron launch delays and deferred revenue recognition.

Launch Complex 1 in New Zealand is critical for Electron cadence. Any geopolitical disruption, regulatory conflict, or relationship deterioration with New Zealand authorities could affect roughly half of Electron launch capacity.

execution.description: Archimedes is a new oxygen/methane engine with no flight heritage. CEO Peter Beck notes the engine must survive 'nasty tests' before Q4 2026 flight. Any propulsion anomaly during qualification resets the timeline and could push first flight into 2027.

Delivering 18 advanced EO/IR-equipped missile-tracking satellites is the largest and most complex program in Rocket Lab history. Schedule or technical performance shortfalls on this contract would damage defense prime credibility and potential future awards.

Integrating Geost's Arizona/Virginia EO/IR operations into Rocket Lab's existing Space Systems infrastructure while scaling production is a complex post-merger execution challenge. Earnout provisions ($50M tied to revenue targets) create additional management pressure.

Founder and CEO Sir Peter Beck is central to Rocket Lab's strategic vision, technical decisions, and investor confidence. No clear succession plan is publicly disclosed. His departure would represent a significant negative catalyst.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Commercial space launch services market is growing rapidly, driven by LEO mega-constellation deployment (Starlink, Kuiper, government PWSA), national security proliferated architectures, and a renaissance in small satellite manufacturing. The global satellite manufacturing market is projected to grow at ~14-15% CAGR through 2035. Rocket Lab is uniquely positioned as the only publicly traded pure-play offering both launch and satellite manufacturing at operational scale.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate cyclicality. U.S. government defense contracts (majority of Space Systems backlog) provide multi-year visibility and reduce cyclicality vs. purely commercial launch. Commercial satellite business is more sensitive to macro and funding cycles. Electron launch demand is underpinned by committed contracted manifests.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: High (indirect) — as a pre-profitability, high-multiple growth company, RKLB's valuation is sensitive to rate-driven multiple compression. Direct balance sheet sensitivity is lower given ~$1.5B cash and minimal debt (~$39M convertible notes after recent conversions).
macro_factors.currency_exposure: Moderate. New Zealand operations expose the company to NZD/USD fluctuations for Electron manufacturing and launch costs. Most contracts are denominated in USD, mitigating revenue-side exposure.
key_input_costs: Carbon fiber composites (Electron and Neutron structure)
EO/IR sensor components and semiconductor content (Geost/Space Systems)
Skilled aerospace and defense engineering labor (tight market)

recent_developments.event: Q1 2026 earnings: Record $200.3M revenue (+63% YoY), 38.2% GAAP gross margin, $2.2B backlog. Q2 2026 guidance set at $225-240M revenue — another record. Company completed 6 Electron/HASTE missions in Q1 2026.

Rocket Lab signed its largest-ever single launch deal with a confidential customer: a bulk order combining multiple Neutron and Electron missions, bringing total launch manifest to 70+ missions and backlog to $2.2B.

Neutron rocket on-ramped to U.S. Space Force's $5.6B NSSL Phase 3 Lane 1 program — one of only five providers eligible to compete for the nation's highest-priority national security launches. Received initial $5M task order for capabilities assessment.
FY2025 10-K filed: Full-year revenue $601.8M (+38% YoY), gross margin 34.4%, operating loss -$228.8M, net loss -$198.2M. Backlog $1.847B at year-end. ESCAPADE Mars spacecraft commissioning confirmed.

Neutron Stage 1 tank failure during pressure testing — a hand-built joint from a third-party contractor failed. Team subsequently redesigned with improved strength margins and manufacturability. First flight target revised from Q1 2026 to Q4 2026.

Awarded $816M prime contract by the Space Development Agency (U.S. Space Force) to build 18 missile-tracking satellites for Tracking Layer Tranche 3 (TRKT3) under PWSA — largest single contract in company history. Combined SDA awards now exceed $1.3B.

Rocket Lab-built ESCAPADE twin spacecraft (Blue and Gold) began Mars journey after November 2025 launch, en route to Mars orbit by September 2027. Demonstrates Photon spacecraft bus capability for interplanetary science missions.

Closed acquisition of Geost (EO/IR sensing systems) for $275M ($125M cash + ~3M shares + $50M earnout). Adds 20+ years of flight-proven electro-optical and infrared sensor heritage for missile warning, ISR, and space domain awareness, completing end-to-end national security space stack.

Set annual record of 21 successful Electron launches in FY2025, including seven in Q4 alone — all with 100% mission success rate. On track to exceed this record in FY2026 and complete the 100th Electron launch.
Stock ran hard through Q1-Q2 2026 from ~$31 in early February 2026 to a 52-week high of ~$151 before settling near $98. Market cap reflecting Neutron and defense prime optionality.

items.notes: Represents 50%+ YoY growth vs. Q2 2025. Implies full-year FY2026 revenue run rate of $900M+ if pace holds. Driven by Space Systems backlog conversion and increasing Electron cadence.
Slightly below Q1 2026's 38.2% due to mix shift — some quarters weighted toward lower-margin hardware deliveries.
Excludes stock-based compensation and depreciation on acquired intangibles.
Continued investment in Neutron development, Geost integration, and Space Systems manufacturing capacity. Breakeven not expected until Neutron reaches commercial cadence.
~36% expected to convert to revenue over the next 12 months (~$790M+ near-term contracted). More than 70 missions in launch manifest.
100th Electron launch expected in FY2026 — would make Rocket Lab the fastest commercial orbital rocket to reach this milestone.

items.vs_prior: maintained (slipped from Q1 2026 after tank failure)
items.notes: CEO Peter Beck: 'on track' but caveated as a rocket program. Archimedes engine qualification is critical path. Five commercial launch contracts already in place for 2026-2029 missions.

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Peter Beck highlighted record Q1 2026 results across all guided metrics and emphasized the $2.2B backlog as evidence of broad demand for both launch and space systems. He characterized Neutron progress as on track for Q4 2026 while acknowledging the inherent uncertainty of rocket development. CFO noted strong gross margin trajectory and reiterated the company's plan to convert a significant portion of its backlog to revenue in 2026 and 2027. Management also highlighted Neutron's NSSL Lane 1 inclusion as validating long-term defense launch opportunity.

bull_case: Neutron is the only credible Western alternative to Falcon 9 in the medium-lift market: with NSSL Lane 1 eligibility ($5.6B program pool), five launch contracts in hand before first flight, and U.S. government preference for non-SpaceX supply chain diversity, a successful Q4 2026 debut opens a multi-billion-dollar addressable market that would transform the company's earnings profile.

Space Systems is already a high-growth business in its own right: FY2025 Space Systems revenue $402.8M (+high double-digits YoY), gross margins expanding, $2.2B backlog providing years of visibility. The $816M SDA TRKT3 contract and >$1.3B total SDA awards anchor the segment through the decade with potential for follow-on tranches and classified programs.

Geost acquisition completes the national security vertical stack: Adding proprietary EO/IR sensor technology to launch + spacecraft manufacturing makes Rocket Lab a genuine end-to-end national security space prime — a rare position among publicly traded companies — enabling bids on classified payload programs previously inaccessible.

Unmatched operational tempo builds durable competitive moat: Record 21 Electron launches in FY2025 with 100% success rate, targeting 100th total launch in FY2026. No small-launch competitor has matched this cadence or reliability. Manufacturing and operations infrastructure at this scale takes a decade to replicate.

Revenue growth trajectory is exceptional and accelerating: FY2025 +38% YoY to $601.8M; Q1 2026 +63% YoY to $200.3M; Q2 2026 guided $225-240M. If Neutron flies and Space Systems continues compounding, $2B+ annual revenue by FY2028 is achievable — at which point the company could approach EBITDA breakeven at scale.
bear_case: Neutron is a high-risk binary event: The Q4 2026 maiden flight has already slipped once (from Q1 2026 after the Stage 1 tank failure) and depends on qualifying the unproven Archimedes engine. Any further delay into 2027 or an anomaly on first flight would shatter the medium-lift thesis and likely trigger a severe derating from a valuation that already prices in substantial Neutron success.

SpaceX's structural dominance may be impossible to overcome on price: Falcon 9 flew 165 times in 2025 (6x all other U.S. providers combined), and SpaceX's Starship program threatens to further collapse launch economics. Neutron's 13,000kg capacity vs. Falcon 9's 17,500kg means it must compete primarily on availability and Western-source preference — a narrower moat than many bulls assume.

The stock has already re-rated dramatically on optionality: Up ~3x from $31 in early February 2026 to ~$98 (52-week high $151), the market cap reflects a very optimistic scenario. Consensus analyst target of ~$103-107 implies near-zero margin of safety. Multiple compression risk is high if any of the key 2026 catalysts (Neutron, SDA execution, margin expansion) disappoints.

Sustained dilution is structural, not episodic: Share count grew from ~505M to ~573M in FY2025 via equity raises; Geost added ~3M more shares; the company will likely need additional capital for Neutron pad construction, Geost earnout, and manufacturing scale. At any price, equity issuance is meaningfully dilutive to existing holders.

Path to GAAP profitability is distant and contingent: Operating loss -$228.8M in FY2025; Adjusted EBITDA guided negative through at least Q2 2026. Breakeven requires Neutron at commercial cadence (3-5 flights/year), full SDA ramp, and continued gross margin expansion — a combination unlikely before 2028 at the earliest, leaving the stock highly vulnerable to sentiment shifts and macro rate moves in the interim.
